what_this_is: How the dossier beside it was shaped, so the reader knows what it is looking at and what it is not. It describes the SHAPING, never the file: every sentence here is the same on every file in every corpus, and nothing in it is evidence.
closed_world: The dossier is the whole of what was sent. There is no document behind it, no page, no filename, no surrounding sentence. A claim can only be anchored in a value that is present in released_evidence.

selection.what_is_offered: observations the local extractors already produced for that version, each addressed by an observation_key and bounded by a span
selection.what_is_never_offered: complete extracted text, whole documents, paths, filenames, OCR output, file hashes, image EXIF, GPS, the person's own typed words, group memberships, and raw sensitive values
selection.ordering: the most placed evidence first -- title, heading and metadata before body -- then a bounded number of the rest
selection.bounded: the count and the length are both capped before the request is built; what did not fit was not sent and is not described

reduction_ladder: none: the dossier fits and is sent unreduced
summarized_facts: facts stand in for their evidence
preserved_anchors: only the anchoring evidence is kept
split: the subject is sent as several dossiers, each judged on its own
reduction_rung_in_force: the dossier's own reduction_rung key says which rung this one was built at
redaction: identifiers the local policy recognises are transformed before the value is written into the dossier. A redacted value is the value that was sent, and it is the only text a citation can quote.
what_is_done_with_the_answer: each claim is checked against the evidence that was actually released -- the field against the allowed vocabulary, the citation against the released value, the value against the cited span, and the whole against any better-supported local fact -- and a claim that fails a check is recorded as having failed it. Nothing here is a hint about which answer passes.
declining: a declined field is recorded as declined and stays open. It is not a failure and it is not counted as one.
